comment: S25 (50 MP): 1/1.56” sensor → Larger individual pixels S25 Ultra (200 MP): 1/1.3” sensor → Much smaller individual pixels The sensor size increase from S25 to S25 Ultra is 1/1.56" to 1/1.3" But the increase in megapixel is 50MP to 200MP ! This is a trick to make it look `better`. If Samsung had kept pixel sizes the same, the S25 Ultra should have had around 60 MP, not 200 MP. The 200 MP resolution is over 3× higher than the proportional sensor increase, which means each individual pixel is significantly smaller. This forces Samsung to rely heavily on pixel binning to improve low-light performance, rather than just using larger native pixels. The MP increase is way out of proportion compared to the sensor size increase. 🚀 Don't fall for that marketing trick. Consider that "200 MP" as "60 MP".
label_notes: Informative technical analysis without emotional language.

comment: My niece was kidnapped from the front yard of her other aunt's house, by a stranger, when she was 4 years old. comment: 2 things worth noting : 1) Bad chargers are not too bad, as you show, there are so many protection circuits and the 2 biggest offenders for LiPos would be stopped there - high voltage and too high current. As long as the charger provides 5v, chances are that there's no risk of current over the specs. If it provides more it would be capped by a regulator. The only bad charger that could get through is one with a big ripple voltage (say from 5 to 3.5) and pulsating on that. This would probably get through the protections and slowly hurt the battery, which likes being charged in a Constant Current then Constant Voltage cycle. 2) In event of failure of all the protection circuits and the "battery abuse" getting through, it would *always* blow up the battery, no matter where the failure was (or if all failed at the same time). So "physical location of the fire" is not a good evidence to where the failure was. But good job showing the dangers and demystifying a bit the phone battery. As usual, respecting the LiPo is the best approach.
label_notes: Informative technical analysis without emotional language.

comment: If anyone wants a summary for their assignment The film is an emotional and heart touching story, about a single father reading a letter written to him by his young daughter. The letter begins as any letter a child would write to her father describing him as smart, sweet and kind. The video shows the dad always smiling, making his daughter laugh. It also shows him walking his daughter to school wearing a suit, buying her ice cream, and tipping the waiter at a restaurant. She says he’s the most handsome dad in the world and calls him her superman. The father expects the rest of the letter to also be words of praise for him from his daughter, but then she writes that he lies. She writes that he lies about having a job and money, he lies about not being tired and not being hungry. The video shows the father not able to find a good job and shows him doing a variety of jobs including washing windows, and doing manual labor. The girl writes that her father lies about being happy all the time and having everything because of her. This makes the father break down in tears and hug his daughter in an emotional scene which touches your heart, and shows the lengths to which fathers will go to give their children the best they possibly can at the cost of their own comfort. The film ends with the message that a child’s future is worth every sacrifice.
label_notes: Describes a heartbreaking story of a father's sacrifices and hidden struggles.

It only covers situations BEFORE boarding where they are Denied Boarding as result of overbooking. It also outline Exceptions (25-A4d), but none of those, in my opinion covers this situation. Only way to get them off once they have boarded must be VOLUNTARY. Which explains their CEO coming out the second time and claiming that the passenger was "belligerent", to use that as an excuse for his removal. Really fucking pathetic.
